newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy February PSBR seen at 8.5 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy February PSBR seen at 8.5 trln lire.

text.p: Italy's public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) in February is expected to stand at 7.5 to 8.5 trillion lire, sharply down from the deficit a year ago, a Reuter poll showed.
Analysts surveyed saw on average a state sector deficit of 8.5 trillion lire against 12.97 trillion in February 1996.
The Italian Treasury has forecast a state sector surplus of two trillion lire for January compared with a deficit of 12.29 trillion in Janaury last year.
This would bring the cumulative deficit for the first two months of 1997 to around 6.5 trillion lire compared with just over 25.0 trillion in the same 1996 period.

But the analysts warned against drawing hasty conclusions about Italy's ability to reach a deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio of 3.0 percent by the end of this year, saying that to have a clearer picture it was necessary to await the quarterly report on state accounts due in April.

However, February's deficit would show a marked improvement. This was mainly due to the government's 62.5 trillion lire budget package for this year drawn up by Prime Minister Romano Prodi at the end of 1996.
The official 1997 PSBR target is 61.4 trillion lire compared with a deficit of 138.5 trillion posted in 1996.

"We forecast the budget's (deficit-cutting) effectiveness at 80 percent, meaning a total of 49.6 trillion lire spread out over the 12 months of this year," said Marcello Esposito of Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI).

Andrea Marchetti of Credito Italiano noted that compared with February 1996, this month would benefit from ministerial spending cuts, lower interest charges of some 1.0 trillion lire and increased state income of about 1.0 trillion lire.
Renzo Avesani of Cariplo agreed, saying "the tighter management of accounts by Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi will have a tangible effect over the whole of this year."

But Lorenzo Codogno of Bank of America did not see any reversal of trend in the Treasury's borrowing needs. "This year will see heavy interest costs for bond coupons falling due as well as the maturity of the first two-year zero coupon certificates (CTZ) issued in February 1995."

The Treasury's forecast for a provisional state sector surplus of two trillion lire at end-January was, it said, due to one-off items including a new form of payment of tax on production of mineral oils and new rules relating to pensions contributing in all some 5.0 trillion lire to state accounts. Cash flows with the European Union were also showing a favourable trend, it noted.
The analysts saw, on average, the need for supplementary budget measures this year of some 17.5 trillion lire.
